summary: This bill amends the Homeland Security Act to require the DHS Science and Technology Directorate to create a department-wide policy and process protecting research and development from unauthorized access or disclosure of sensitive information in acquisitions, plus a GAO report on DHS compliance with related national security guidance and a congressional briefing.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Homeland Security Act to add a new duty for the Under Secretary of Science and Technology to develop a department-wide policy and process for safeguarding R&D from unauthorized access or disclosure. It also requires a GAO report and a congressional briefing. These are administrative mandates without specific appropriations, so any implied spending increase is minimal and tangential, not a clear expansion or reduction of government spending.
The bill makes no mention of taxes, tax rates, or tax policy whatsoever. It focuses solely on research security policies within DHS.
No provisions related to healthcare, coverage, or medical policy. The bill is about DHS research security.
No references to guns, firearms, or regulations on weapons.

While DHS handles immigration, this bill specifically addresses research and development security in the Science and Technology Directorate, with no connection to immigration enforcement, borders, or pathways.
No relation to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill concerns DHS research security, not military or defense spending. DHS S&T may support security tech, but it does not increase or decrease defense budgets or military activities.
No environmental protections, regulations, or climate-related provisions.
No impact on welfare, food stamps, or social programs.
No connection to schools, education funding, or policy.
No provisions on drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill addresses unauthorized access to research info, but not criminal justice reform, sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation.
No mention of trade, tariffs, or protectionism.
No focus on deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy. Administrative mandates do not meaningfully affect debt.
No provisions affecting LGBTQ+ protections or rights.
No relation to foreign aid spending or programs.
No impact on voting access, elections, or integrity measures.

The core of the bill requires developing policies and processes to safeguard sensitive information in DHS R&D from unauthorized access or disclosure, directly enhancing data protection and oversight in government research acquisitions. It also mandates reporting on compliance with national research security guidance (NSPM-33). This has a moderate, clear impact toward more oversight and data protection in the tech/research security domain.
No worker protections, unions, or labor policy mentioned.
No provisions on religious exemptions, civil rights, or discrimination.
